name: Travel Air 2000 / 4000 Biplane
variants: Travel Air D-4000 / E-4000 (Wright J-5 / Whirlwind)
summary: Barnstorming-era open-cockpit biplane of the late 1920s; the Model 4000 family has a rugged steel-tube fuselage and was a staple of early commercial flying.

wings: Single-bay staggered biplane braced with N-struts
Large 'elephant ear' ailerons with overhanging balance horns
engines: Radial engine (Wright J-5 or similar), or a water-cooled OX-5 V-8 with a nose radiator on early models
fuselage: Two tandem open cockpits with the front one wide enough for two
Fixed tailskid gear, with oleo outrigger on some variants

tellTales: Biplane with big elephant-ear ailerons overhanging the wing tips
1920s open-cockpit biplane with a radial or V-8 engine
N-strut bracing and a wide front cockpit

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stearman is a later, larger design without the overhanging balanced ailerons; the Travel Air has distinctive horn-balanced ailerons.
The Waco 10 has strut-linked upper and lower ailerons without big overhanging horns.
The Waco F-series has a smoother, later-style fuselage and wide-track gear; the Travel Air is a boxier 1920s design.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
